judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys both evaluate to the duplicate literal "[object Object]" (z.string().toString() is "[object Object]"), so the second entry overwrites the first and the promised "any property with a number is the expiry" validation does not exist. In sharing mode the schema validates only access_token; responses with no expiry field pass validation, expiry_date/expires_in are never persisted, and every calendar operation re-runs the refresh flow (a per-operation POST to the sync endpoint) because the stored token always appears expired.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines two computed keys using `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()`. Those are runtime string keys, and both evaluate to the same string (effectively `"[object Object]"`), so the latter overwrites the former. As a result, the schema does not enforce “any numeric expiry field” at all and (because Zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default) it will also drop fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in` from the returned `.data` in sharing mode. This matches the finding that sharing-mode validation degenerates to essentially just `access_token` and can fail to persist expiry information.
